newsitem.title: USA: Rally's moving away from discount strategy.
newsitem.headline: Rally's moving away from discount strategy.

text.p: In an effort to regain lost customers and reopen some stores it was forced to shut, Rally's Hamburgers Inc is moving away from its discount strategy in favor of proven advertising and quality programs, President and Chief Executive Officer Don Doyle said.

Speaking at the Cruttenden Roth Growth Stock conference here, Doyle said the shift has already started to improve bottom line results, although it has resulted in lower same store sales at some locations.

"We're convinced the constant price cuts cheepened our brand," Doyle said. "And with every hamburger chain offering 99 cent burgers, discounts were no longer a compelling reason for the customer to drive past the competition."

The new strategy, he said, is to position Rally's "as the quick service restaurant for great burgers." Because the company is 18 percent owned by CKE Restaurants Inc, it is able to use that chain's highly successful Carl's Jr. hamburger commercials by simply dubbing in the Rally's name and slogan. Doyle said advertising spending will be "significantly higher" in 1997, and will be based on "a library of proven Carl's Jr. commercials."
